subtype: Approach: uses waiting as a way to avoid a needed decision [Pitfall]
passage:
In the Class 12 counselling room, Aparna slid the two course forms across the desk. "The last date is the fifteenth. Have you picked?"

Santosh shrugged. "I'll sleep on it."

A week later he said it again, and the week after that. Each time Aparna asked what he had found out, he said, "Nothing new, I'm still thinking." He had not opened either college website or asked a senior about the hostel. On the sixteenth he came in with the forms still unsigned and read the notice on the board.

"It closed yesterday." He stared at the paper. "I thought more time would just make it clear."

Aparna pulled a chair up beside him and asked what he wanted to do about it now.

qa.q: On which date had the forms closed?
qa.a: The forms closed on the fifteenth, the day before Santosh read the notice.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling as he read the notice on the board?
qa.a: Santosh was shocked and probably regretful, staring at the paper after hoping that more time would make things clear.

qa.q: What could Santosh have done with those weeks instead of only waiting?
qa.a: Santosh could have set a date to decide, opened the college websites and asked a senior about the hostel, so there were new facts to think about.

qa.q: How might Aparna have felt each time Santosh said he would sleep on it?
qa.a: Aparna may have felt concerned and a little helpless, seeing nothing new gathered while the last date came closer.

grounding: Shows a student using 'sleeping on it' with no end date and gathering nothing, so a deadline passes.
